chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who did not know whether he had circumambulated six or seven, he said: He should do it again.

key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلُ: He should do it again / face it again (perform another circuit)

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they are unsure whether they completed six or seven circuits of Tawaf?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the doubt of a pilgrim uncertain whether they completed six or seven circuits of Tawaf by instructing them to perform one additional circuit (*istiqbal*). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of treating the lower number as the baseline to ensure the obligatory seven circuits are fulfilled, reflecting the precautionary approach (*ihtiyat*) in ritual purity and worship. It underscores the importance of certainty in completing the pillars of Hajj, a core theme in Shia fiqh derived from the Imams' precise legal interpretations.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who did not know whether he had circumambulated six (circuits) or seven. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should do it again’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “About a man who does not know if he has performed six or seven Tawaf (walking around the House), abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
has said, ‘He must do his Tawaf again.’”
